name: Amritsari Fish
ingredients: 500g firm white fish fillets (sole or singhara)
instructions: 1. Cut the fish into 2-inch long strips and pat dry. 2. Marinate the fish with salt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and red chili powder for 20 minutes. 3. In a bowl, combine gram flour, rice flour, carom seeds, turmeric, and the egg to form a thick, smooth batter. 4. Coat the fish pieces thoroughly in the batter. 5. Heat oil in a deep pan and deep-fry the fish on medium-high heat until golden brown and crispy. 6. Remove, drain excess oil, sprinkle generously with chaat masala, and serve hot with mint chutney.
description: Amritsari Fish is an iconic North Indian street food originating from the Punjab region. It is a staple in Chandigarh's vibrant food scene, famous for its signature crunch provided by the gram flour batter and the distinct digestive punch of ajwain (carom seeds). It represents the hearty, robust culinary tradition of the Punjabi people.
